terms.meaning: A small automatic check that runs one piece of code and confirms the result is what was expected.
The testing tool that comes with Python, so no extra install is needed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and import path
sections.what: Adds the scripts folder to the import path and loads the search, design system and saving functions that the tests need.
sections.why: Lets the tests run from any folder without installing the project.
sections.watch_out: The tests depend on the folder layout, so moving this file breaks the path setup.

sections.name: TestTokenizer
sections.title: Word handling checks
sections.what: Checks that short technical words such as UI, 3D and AI are kept, that common filler words are removed, and that hyphenated words match their unhyphenated forms.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: keeping these words stops searches from silently losing useful terms.
sections.watch_out: The hyphen test depends on the exact word rules in the tokenizer, so changing those rules will break it.

sections.name: TestSearchDomains
sections.title: Search coverage checks
sections.what: Checks that style and accessibility queries return results, that nonsense queries return zero results with suggestions, and that every domain and stack answers a basic query without error.
sections.why: Confirms every configured data file can be loaded and searched.
sections.watch_out: These checks confirm there is no error, not that the results are the right ones.

sections.name: TestDomainDetection
sections.title: Domain routing checks
sections.what: Checks that style words route to the style domain, accessibility words route to the ux domain, and an empty or symbol-only query falls back to style.
sections.why: Routing decides which data file answers a query when the user does not name a domain.
sections.watch_out: The runner-up check only confirms the call works, so it would not notice a wrong runner-up.

sections.name: TestPersistence
sections.title: Design system saving checks
sections.what: Checks that saving creates the master file, that a second save without force leaves it unchanged, that force overwrites it, and that files only land under the chosen output folder.
sections.why: Protects existing design decisions from being overwritten by accident.
sections.watch_out: The tests use temporary folders, so they never touch the real project files.

sections.name: TestReasoningMatch
sections.title: Reasoning rule lookup checks
sections.what: Checks that a known category name finds its rule and that an unknown name returns an empty result instead of crashing.
sections.why: The reasoning rules decide the default look for each product category, so a failed lookup would give poor defaults.
sections.watch_out: The first check only asserts that a value is returned, so it would not notice a wrong rule.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Running the test file directly
sections.what: Lets you run every test in this file by running it as a program. The standard test runner finds the test classes in the file, runs them, and prints a pass or fail summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: the usual way to make a Python test file runnable on its own. Reason not stated in the code beyond that.

summary: Automatic checks that confirm the search, domain-detection and design-system saving code still behave as expected.
purpose: Protects the core search engine of the design helper from silent breakage when its data or code changes.
why: Likely reason: the project ships with no outside libraries, so the tests use only the standard Python test tools to keep it that way.
how: 1) Adds the scripts folder to the import path. 2) Runs groups of checks for word handling, domain searches, domain detection and file saving. 3) Each check compares a real result with an expected result and fails loudly if they differ.
inputs: The data files used by the search engine and the design-system generator. The tests create their own temporary folders for saved output.
outputs: A pass or fail report for each check, printed when the tests run.
risks: Searches check that some result exists, not the exact best result, so ranking bugs may pass unnoticed. The last test group is cut off in the view used for this note, so its checks could not be confirmed.
debug: Run the tests with the unittest command given at the top of the file. If a search check fails, look at the matching data file and the search code in core. If a save check fails, check the output folder logic in design_system.
